summary: Native-addon dropper decrypts and executes opaque payload on require()
details: evt-dispatcher@1.0.4 presents itself as a trivial event-dispatcher library, but index.js side-effectfully loads two shipped native binaries (native_win.node, native.napi.node) at require() time with three redundant try/catch requires that are unrelated to the pure-JS EventBus class the package otherwise exports. The native modules contain format strings '%s\.napi_cache', '%s.nc%lu.js', and 'node "%s"', consistent with decoding the 1.3MB opaque.napi_cache blob shipped in the package root into a JavaScript file and spawning node to execute it. The native binaries also contain sandbox/CI detection (GITHUB_ACTIONS, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, SANDBOX, /proc/1/cgroup, docker/containerd/kubepod/podman), debugger checks (IsDebuggerPresent, CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent, TracerPid), analyst-tool enumeration (wireshark, procmon, procexp, x64dbg, ollydbg, fiddler, httpdebug), and Linux daemonization via fork+setsid+_exit. The 1,325,877-byte.napi_cache ships with zero printable strings, consistent with an encrypted payload. The declared EventBus functionality is self-contained and never interacts with the native modules, so the native loader is pure cover-driven install/import-time code execution on any machine that requires this package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
